'''Victoria Ruth Neale''' (March 1984 – 3 May 2023)<ref name=mactutor/> was a British mathematician and writer. She was Whitehead Lecturer at [[University of Oxford|Oxford]]'s [[Mathematical Institute, University of Oxford|Mathematical Institute]] and Supernumerary Fellow at [[Balliol College]].<ref name="homepage">{{Cite web|url=http://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/neale/|title=Homepage|last=Neale|first=Vicky|date=2018-08-03|website=[[Mathematical Institute, University of Oxford]]|language=en|access-date=2018-08-07}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.acme-uk.org/events/2016-acme-conference/speakers-and-panellists|title=Speakers and Panellists - ACME|website=[[Advisory Committee on Mathematics Education]]|access-date=2018-08-07|archive-date=10 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180810205137/http://www.acme-uk.org/events/2016-acme-conference/speakers-and-panellists|url-status=dead}}<br/>{{cite web |url=https://www.bcme.org.uk/Plenary-Speakers |title=BCME 9 Plenary Speakers |website=[[Mathematical Association|British Congress of Mathematics Education]] |date=2018 |access-date=2018-08-10 }}</ref> Her research specialty was [[number theory]]. The author of the 2017 book ''[[Closing the Gap: The Quest to Understand Prime Numbers]]'',<ref>{{cite book|last=Neale |first=Vicky |title=Closing the Gap: The Quest to Understand Prime Numbers |publisher=[[Oxford University Press]] |isbn=9780198788287 |oclc=1030559953|year=2017 }}</ref><ref>Reviews of ''Closing the Gap'' include the following:
*{{Cite web|url=https://www.maa.org/press/maa-reviews/closing-the-gap|title=Closing the Gap {{!}} Mathematical Association of America|last=Hunacek|first=Mark|date=2018-02-12|website=[[Mathematical Association of America]]|language=en|access-date=2018-08-07|archive-date=28 September 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200928070952/https://www.maa.org/press/maa-reviews/closing-the-gap|url-status=dead}}
*{{Cite news|url=https://plus.maths.org/content/closing-gap|title='Closing the gap'|last=Freiberger|first=Marianne|date=2017-12-12|work=[[Plus Magazine]]|access-date=2018-08-07|language=en}}
*{{Cite news|url=http://euro-math-soc.eu/review/closing-gap|title=Review: Closing the Gap|publisher=European Mathematical Society|date=February 2018|accessdate=2018-09-10|first=Adhemar|last=Bultheel|authorlink=Adhemar Bultheel|archive-date=11 September 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180911044635/http://euro-math-soc.eu/review/closing-gap|url-status=dead}}
*{{Cite news|url=http://chalkdustmagazine.com/blog/closing-the-gap/|title=Closing the Gap|last=Kalaydzhieva|first=Nikoleta|date=2018-06-28|work=[[Chalkdust (magazine)|Chalkdust]]|access-date=2018-08-07|last2=Porritt|first2=Sam|language=en-GB}}
*{{Cite journal|last=Fried|first=Michael N.|date=2018-07-03|title=Prime Numbers, Mathematical Pencils, and Massive Collaboration|journal=Mathematical Thinking and Learning|language=en|volume=20|issue=3|pages=248–250|doi=10.1080/10986065.2018.1483932|issn=1098-6065}}</ref> she was interviewed on several [[BBC]] radio programs as a mathematics expert.<ref>Among her appearances are the following:
*{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/b01ngn3j|title=Fermat's Last Theorem, In Our Time - BBC Radio 4|website=BBC|language=en-GB|access-date=2018-08-07}}
*{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/b048jmy9|title=Numbers Numbers Everywhere, Series 10, The Infinite Monkey Cage - BBC Radio 4|website=BBC|language=en-GB|access-date=2018-08-07}}
*{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/b04hz49f|title=e, In Our Time - BBC Radio 4|website=BBC|language=en-GB|access-date=2018-08-07}}
*{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/b04p87s4|title=Vicky Neale on the Mathematics of Beauty, A History of Ideas - BBC Radio 4|website=BBC|language=en-GB|access-date=2018-08-07}}
*{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/b084df9c|title=Maths: Alex Bellos, Neil deGrasse Tyson, Serafina Cuomo, Vicky Neale, Free Thinking - BBC Radio 3|website=BBC|language=en-GB|access-date=2018-08-07}}</ref><ref>She is also quoted as a mathematics expert in, for example,
*{{Cite web|url=https://newhumanist.org.uk/articles/5208/what-makes-maths-beautiful |title=What Makes Maths Beautiful? |last=Flyn |first=Cal|author-link=Cal Flyn |date=2017-07-10 |access-date=2018-08-10 |website=[[New Humanist]]}}
*{{Cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/science/2016/nov/21/magic-numbers-can-maths-equations-be-beautiful |last=Sample |first=Ian |title=Magic numbers: can maths equations be beautiful? |website=[[The Guardian]] |access-date=2018-08-10 |date=2016-11-21}}</ref> In addition, she wrote for [[The Conversation (website)|''The Conversation'']] and ''[[The Guardian]]''.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://theconversation.com/mathematics-is-beautiful-no-really-72921|title=Mathematics is beautiful (no, really)|last=Neale|first=Vicky|date=2017-02-17|work=[[The Conversation (website)|The Conversation]]|access-date=2018-08-07|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/science/alexs-adventures-in-numberland/2015/nov/26/solving-for-xmas-how-to-make-mathematical-christmas-cards|title=Solving for Xmas: how to make mathematical Christmas cards|last=Neale|first=Vicky|date=2015-11-26|website=[[The Guardian]]|language=en|access-date=2018-08-07}}</ref> Her other educational and outreach activities included lecturing at the PROMYS Europe high-school program<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.claymath.org/library/annual_report/ar2016.pdf|title=Annual Report 2016|date=2017-06-26|website=[[Clay Mathematics Institute]]|access-date=2018-08-07}}</ref> and helping to organize the [[European Girls' Mathematical Olympiad]].<ref name="promys">{{Cite web|url=https://promys-europe.org/about-promys-europe/faculty|title=Principal Faculty {{!}} PROMYS-Europe: Program in Mathematics for Young Scientists|website=promys-europe.org|language=en|access-date=2018-08-07}}</ref>

Neale was born in 1984.<ref>[https://www.balliol.ox.ac.uk/news/2023/may/vicky-neale-1984-2023 Vicky Neale 1984–2023], [[Balliol College]]</ref> She obtained her PhD in 2011 from the [[University of Cambridge]]. Her thesis work, supervised by [[Ben Green (mathematician)|Ben Joseph Green]], concerned [[Waring's problem]].<ref name="homepage"/><ref name=genealogy>{{MathGenealogy|id=175723}}</ref> She then taught at Cambridge while being Director of Studies in mathematics at [[Murray Edwards College, Cambridge|Murray Edwards College]],<ref name="promys"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://gowers.wordpress.com/2014/01/11/introduction-to-cambridge-ia-analysis-i-2014/ |title=Introduction to Cambridge IA Analysis I 2014 |last=Gowers |first=Timothy |author-link=Timothy Gowers |website=Gowers' Weblog |date=2014-01-11 |access-date=2018-08-10}}</ref> before moving to Oxford in the summer of 2014.<ref>{{cite news|work=Floreat Domus 2015 |publisher=Balliol College |title=Balliol Maths: a plurality of women |url=https://issuu.com/balliol/docs/floreat_domus_2015/33 |access-date=2018-08-10}}</ref> 

Neale died on 3 May 2023, at the age of 39.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-05-04 |title=Vicky Neale {{!}} Mathematical Institute |url=https://www.maths.ox.ac.uk/node/64230 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230504171021/https://www.maths.ox.ac.uk/node/64230 |archive-date=2023-05-04 |access-date=2023-05-04 |website=Mathematical Institute, University of Oxford}}</ref> She had been diagnosed with a rare type of cancer in 2021.<ref>[https://www.lms.ac.uk/node/2116 Dr Vicky Neale (1984-2023)], [[London Mathematical Society]]</ref>
